raw_segments.text: It was not in the first few moments that I saw all these things, though I saw more of
them in the first moments than might be supposed. But I saw that everything within my view which
ought to be white had been white long ago, and had lost its luster and was faded and
yellow. I saw that the bride within the bridal dress had withered like the dress, and like
the flowers, and had no brightness left but the brightness of her sunken eyes.
I saw that the dress had been put upon the rounded figure of a young woman, and that
the figure upon which it now hung loose had shrunk to skin and bone. Once, I had been
taken to see some ghastly waxwork at the fair, representing I know not what impossible personage
lying in state. Once, I had been taken to one of our old marsh churches to see a skeleton
in the ashes of a rich dress that had been dug out of a vault under the church pavement.
Now, waxwork and skeletons seemed to have dark eyes that moved and looked at me. I should
have cried out if I could.
